options.content:
**All PVCs share one disk.**
k3s uses the local-path provisioner, so every claim is a
directory on the node's root filesystem (`/dev/sda2`).

They therefore all report the *same* utilisation — it is
the root disk's, not the claim's. A PVC here has no
independent size limit, and one runaway writer fills
every volume at once.

Watch **Root disk** in the health strip; the per-PVC
rows are only useful for spotting which claim is
growing, via the write rate rather than the level.

panels.description: Fullest Cilium BPF map on any node (entries / max entries). Conntrack and NAT maps are sized in terraform-aws-k8s-ha cilium.tf (ctTcpMax/natMax 2097152). Near 100% new connections fail to get an entry and are dropped -- the #38 failure mode.

panels.description: Live conntrack entries per node after each GC pass, by family and protocol. Compare with ctTcpMax/ctAnyMax: a curve approaching the limit precedes map-full drops.
panels.title: Conntrack entries alive after GC

panels.description: Datapath drops whose reason is a conntrack or NAT insertion failure. Non-zero means a map was full -- the matching cilium-agent warnings are in the Logs dashboard.
